meta.description: Complete automated literature discovery pipeline: multi-source search → six-dimension scoring → fine reading → formatted delivery → archival. Combines configurable engine with daily cron-driven application layer. Works with Feishu, Telegram, or any messaging platform. Production-tested with safeguards (score validation, triple de-dup, graceful degradation).

scientific_integrity.detail: Score validation enforced (dimensions capped, totals recalculated, no inflation). Triple de-duplication (DOI/arXiv ID/OpenAlex ID) prevents redundancy. Source level tagging (full-text/abstract/metadata) maintains transparency.

practice_boundaries.detail: Appropriate scope for automated literature monitoring. Read-only archive safeguard (writes to raw/ only, wiki integration manual) prevents unauthorized knowledge base modification. Keyword drift warning reminds users to review monthly.

methodological_ground.detail: Six-dimension scoring system sound (topic match, methodology, journal quality, network relevance, applied value, archival value). Graceful degradation to backup sources maintains coverage. Gap analysis methodology documented.

code_usability.detail: Complete pipeline with config template (literature-push-template.md). Cron setup documentation provided. Note template with YAML frontmatter standardizes output. Related skills integration documented.

functional_suitability.note: Comprehensive pipeline: multi-source search (arXiv/OpenAlex/Crossref/Semantic Scholar), six-dimension scoring with coarse filter (30→5), fine reading with source-level tagging, formatted delivery to multiple platforms, archival with de-dup. Gap analysis and review compilation workflows. Minor: no explicit retrospective search (backfill historical literature).

reliability.note: Excellent safeguards: score validation (dimensions capped, totals recalculated), triple de-duplication (DOI/arXiv/OpenAlex), graceful degradation (Semantic Scholar down → auto-switch), read-only archive (raw/ only), source-level tagging prevents misleading claims about access.

performance_context.note: Efficient coarse filter reduces 30 candidates to top 5 for fine reading. Cron-driven daily automation. Auto-degradation maintains availability. Minor: no explicit guidance for rate-limit handling during multi-source search bursts.

agent_usability.note: Clear two-layer architecture (engine vs application). Configurable keywords, scoring weights, classification rules, delivery target, archive path. Config template provided. Cron setup documented. Minor: lacks explicit decision tree for choosing scoring weights by research field (experimental vs theoretical, applied vs fundamental).

human_usability.note: Excellent quick-start guidance. Formatted digest with emoji markers (🏅 rank, ⭐ score, 💡 one-liner, 🔬 methods, 📊 results, 🧭 commentary). Bilingual keyword support. Pitfalls section warns about keyword drift, score inflation, duplicate creep, wiki safety, cron locality.

security.note: Read-only archive safeguard prevents unauthorized wiki modification. Cron locality clearly stated (local, not cloud). API keys managed externally (no hardcoding). Minor: no explicit guidance for handling delivery platform credentials (Feishu bot token, Telegram API key).

maintainability.note: Excellent modular design: engine (scoring, classification, templates) separate from application (cron, delivery, archival). Config template externalizes domain-specific content. Related skills integration documented. Minor: lacks version tracking for config schema (weights, classification rules) across updates.

agent_specific.note: Strong pipeline orchestration. Score validation prevents inflation. Source-level tagging. Graceful degradation. Minor: no explicit subagent management strategy for parallel fine reading of top 5 papers. Cron locality limitation (machine must be running) not addressed with cloud alternatives.

key_strengths: Excellent safeguards: score validation prevents inflation, triple de-duplication (DOI/arXiv/OpenAlex), graceful degradation maintains availability
Strong modular architecture: engine (scoring, classification, templates) separate from application (cron, delivery, archival) enables customization
Robust quality control: read-only archive (raw/ only) prevents unauthorized wiki modification, source-level tagging maintains transparency

Production-tested design: pitfalls section documents real operational issues (keyword drift, score inflation, duplicate creep, wiki safety, cron locality)

recommendations.title: Add cloud-based cron alternatives documentation
recommendations.problem: Cron locality limitation (machine must be running) acknowledged but no alternative solutions provided. Users with laptops/desktops that sleep or travel cannot maintain daily pipeline without constant uptime.
recommendations.root_cause: Hermes cron is local-only. Cloud alternatives (GitHub Actions, AWS Lambda, Google Cloud Scheduler) not documented.
recommendations.fix: Add references/cloud-deployment.md with: (1) GitHub Actions workflow template (runs on schedule in cloud), (2) AWS Lambda + EventBridge setup, (3) Google Cloud Scheduler configuration, (4) comparison table (cost, reliability, setup complexity). Include migration guide from local cron to cloud.

recommendations.title: Add scoring weight decision tree by research field
recommendations.problem: Six-dimension scoring weights configurable but no guidance on choosing weights for different research fields. Experimental biology, theoretical CS, applied engineering have different priorities (methodology vs application vs archival value).
recommendations.root_cause: Scoring system documented with default weights but lacks field-specific recommendations.
recommendations.fix: Add references/field-specific-weights.md with: (1) decision tree: experimental → high methodology (25-30), theoretical → high archival (20-25), applied → high applied value (25-30), (2) example weight profiles for 5-6 common fields, (3) validation heuristics (sum to 100%, no dimension <5%). Include in config template as commented examples.

recommendations.title: Add parallel fine-reading strategy with subagent management
recommendations.problem: Fine reading of top 5 papers done sequentially. For papers with full-text access, reading time can be significant (2-3 min per paper = 10-15 min total). No guidance for parallel subagent dispatch to speed up this bottleneck.
recommendations.root_cause: Pipeline documentation focuses on sequential steps. Agent-specific capabilities (parallel execution) not explicitly leveraged in fine-reading phase.
recommendations.fix: Add references/parallel-fine-reading.md documenting: (1) dispatch 5 subagents in parallel, one per paper, (2) timeout handling (3 min per paper, fail gracefully for slow full-text), (3) result aggregation with partial-success mode (deliver 4/5 if one times out), (4) token budget management (estimate 50k per paper for full-text). Update pipeline workflow diagram to show parallel fine-reading phase.
